commands.notes: grep default BRE; -E ERE; egrep is grep -E and fgrep is grep -F; differing -E/-F/-P/dialect aliases are a conflicting-matchers usage error (status 2). -x anchors each pattern to the whole line; -f FILE reads LF-separated patterns from a pinned file (an empty file selects nothing). rg default RE2-compatible regex. -F exact bytes; -P uses pcre-common-v1 declared grammar; P13 selects/qualifies engine/adapter from regex.json. grep recursive includes hidden but respects explicit exclusions; rg default ignore/hidden rules reuse owner, -u increments ignore bypass, --hidden enables hidden, no symlink traversal beyond authorized selected -R. Unreadable/capped inputs are error/incomplete, never no-match. No args uses stdin except rg --files inventory. Output lines are PATH:LINE:TEXT for matches and PATH-LINE-TEXT for context; the path prefix appears for multiple or recursive inputs unless --no-filename (or grep -h), the line field only with -n, and -- separates non-adjacent context groups. -o prints each match as its own line with the same prefixes; -l/-L/-c print one LF-terminated path or PATH:COUNT record. No NUL-delimited path form is offered. A file holding NUL bytes is binary (GNU 3.5+ form): a selected output line prints 'grep: PATH: binary file matches' once on stderr and the file stops; -c/-l/-L/-q count normally. Recursion visits names in unsigned byte order. -b prefixes the byte offset of each line (of each match with -o); -Z ends file names with NUL instead of ':' or LF; -z reads and writes NUL-terminated records; -T right-aligns numbers to the digit count of the input's size and puts a TAB before content; --line-buffered is accepted (output is already exact); --color=never|auto prints plain text (stdout is never a terminal) and --color=always refuses. GNU, BSD and busybox spellings with one meaning are all accepted: -a/--text searches binary data as text; -I and --binary-files=without-match treat binary files as holding no match; --binary-files=binary|text select the default or -a; -G is the default BRE; -y is -i; --silent is -q; -NUM is -C NUM; -d read|skip|recurse and -D read|skip choose directory and device handling; BSD --include-dir descends only into matching directories; BSD -S follows every link under -R, -p and -O none beyond the command line; -u, -U/--binary and --mmap change nothing; --label names standard input. -Z stays GNU's --null (BSD's decompression spelling would mean something else); BSD -J, -X and -M decompressors are refused.

GNU-only --include/--exclude forms are accepted portable extensions with same stated filtering, not claimed stock ripgrep aliases. rg honours .gitignore, .ignore and the project's ignore rules by default; --no-ignore drops them (as -u does) while still skipping hidden entries; -T excludes a catalogued file type; --color=never|auto prints plain text and --color=always refuses. --json prints ripgrep 15's JSON Lines: begin, match and context messages per file with output, its end message with statistics and one closing summary; field order, escaping, {"bytes"} base64 data and statistics follow rg, elapsed times are this search's own; listing and counting forms ignore --json as rg does. Without PATH operands rg searches an attached stdin (a pipe or redirect) and walks the current directory when no producer is attached, as ripgrep does.

commands.notes: Default . and implicit -print if no action. Boolean !/-not > implicit/-a > -o; parenthesis group; short-circuit. -type f|d|l, -size signed count in c bytes/k KiB/M MiB/default512-byte blocks; -mtime N compares whole days since modification (truncated) against N, +N greater, -N less; -newer FILE is a strictly later modification time than FILE's; name/path shell patterns, regex ERE whole path. -prune stops descend, -delete depth-first recoverable P16 rm. -exec CMD ... {} ; exact single or {} + serial batched argv through normal binder; delimiters are AST words, no reparsing. -R symlink recursion absent. -iregex is -regex with Unicode simple case folding; -mmin is -mtime in minutes; -perm MODE matches exact octal permission bits, -MODE all of them and /MODE any of them; -user takes a numeric uid (names are not resolved) and refuses where the platform has no POSIX owners; -printf supports %p %f %h %P %s %d %y %m %U %G %T@ %% and the escapes \n \t \0 \\, refusing other directives. GNU, BSD and busybox spellings with one meaning are all accepted: BSD's leading -E (extended -regex, already the dialect) and -s (sorted, already the order); -x, -xdev and -mount stay on the starting point's device; -P never follows links (the default), -H follows command-line links and -L/-follow every contained link with loop detection (a followed link is its target, so -type l then matches only unreachable links); -d and -depth visit depth first, and BSD's -depth N is a depth test when a number follows; -amin, -cmin, -atime and -ctime are -mmin/-mtime over access and change times; -uid, -gid and -group take numeric ids; -and, -or, -true and -false; -type also takes p, s, b and c; -size also takes w (2-byte words), G, T and P. -newerXY REF is true when the entry's X time (a access, m modification, c change) is strictly later than REF's Y time, or than the date REF when Y is t; dates use the date -d grammar in the program TZ.

commands.notes: tree 2.x over the held roots through the search walk: entries in unsigned byte order with UTF-8 branches, links shown as NAME -> TARGET and not followed, hidden names only with -a. -L limits depth, -d lists directories only, -f prints paths from the operand, -I excludes and -P selects file names by wildcard patterns joined with |. --gitignore applies the project ignore owner, the same view rg and the source catalog use. The report counts listed directories (the operand when it lists anything) and files; --noreport omits it and -J prints tree's JSON. Entries the read boundary protects are never listed; walks over traversal_visits refuse.
